prompts.text:
Work through the following four independent engineering cases in order. Keep their assumptions separate, identify cross-case lessons only after each analysis, and finish with a short synthesis that does not invent tool results.

Calibration case 1 of 4. Treat this as an independent repository task; preserve its constraints and reason through concrete evidence before the next case.

Act as a repository coding agent investigating a correctness regression in a distributed inference service. You may inspect files, search symbols, run read-only diagnostics, patch code, and execute focused tests. A request enters an HTTP handler, receives a request identifier, is indexed by a scheduler, and is later materialized into a GPU batch. After a recent refactor, two concurrent requests occasionally exchange their stop conditions even though their generated tokens remain separate. The suspicious code stores stop conditions in a process-global dictionary keyed by a reusable pool slot. Explain how you would trace the request identity across modules before editing anything. Identify the invariants that should hold when pool slots are recycled. Propose a minimal typed design that binds stop conditions to an immutable request generation rather than a bare slot. Include a small pseudocode patch, tests for slot reuse and concurrent cancellation, and commands you would run to rule out unrelated failures. Distinguish evidence from inference throughout. Do not invent file contents or claim tests ran when they did not. Finish with a concise handoff describing the likely root cause, the safest fix boundary, and any remaining race that requires a stress test.

Calibration case 2 of 4. Treat this as an independent repository task; preserve its constraints and reason through concrete evidence before the next case.

You are optimizing a CUDA inference kernel for two Ampere GPUs while preserving CUDA graph replay safety. The decode path reads a byte-packed two-bit latent cache, reconstructs groups with asymmetric scale and zero metadata, computes sparse attention, and updates one online softmax. Current throughput is limited by memory traffic and launch overhead at batch sizes one through six. Build a measurement-driven optimization plan for SM86. Discuss how to separate cache bandwidth, unpack cost, matrix instructions, synchronization, and inter-GPU communication using counters and controlled variants. The graph contract requires stable tensor addresses, no host synchronization, no data-dependent allocation, and identical behavior during speculative verification. Suggest two kernel layouts, including warp ownership, vectorized loads, metadata reuse, and accumulation precision. Explain when fusing dequantization into the consumer should win and when register pressure could erase that gain. Provide parity cases covering extreme quantization codes, degenerate scales, ragged page tails, protected recent-window rows, and replay with changing logical lengths. State clear rejection criteria for an optimization that is faster but changes numerics or silently falls back to another cache format. End with a prioritized experiment table described in prose, including expected signal and rollback condition for each experiment.

Calibration case 3 of 4. Treat this as an independent repository task; preserve its constraints and reason through concrete evidence before the next case.

Diagnose an asynchronous Python service where shutdown sometimes hangs after all client requests appear complete. The service owns a scheduler task, a bounded work queue, two worker tasks, and a metrics exporter. Cancellation currently places a sentinel into the queue and immediately awaits every task with gather. One worker can be blocked publishing a final metric because the exporter has already stopped consuming. Construct a precise event timeline for the deadlock and identify which observations would confirm it. Then design a structured-concurrency shutdown protocol with explicit ownership, idempotent close behavior, bounded draining, and meaningful exception handling. Provide typed pseudocode using asyncio primitives without broad exception swallowing. Explain how backpressure should behave before and during shutdown, and whether unfinished work should be cancelled or completed under a configurable grace period. Design deterministic tests using events rather than sleeps, including simultaneous close calls, a full queue, an exporter failure, and cancellation during result publication. Mention how to inspect live task stacks without changing external state. Finally, discuss how the solution changes if workers run in separate processes and queue operations cross a serialization boundary. Keep the answer grounded in the stated system and label any assumption that would need repository evidence.

Calibration case 4 of 4. Treat this as an independent repository task; preserve its constraints and reason through concrete evidence before the next case.

Analyze a Rust peer-to-peer control plane built around immutable events and an elected coordinator. Each node publishes local events, the coordinator assigns a global sequence number, and workers apply indexed events to state. During coordinator failover, a delayed message from the prior term can be indexed by the new coordinator with a fresh sequence number, duplicating a model launch. Develop a protocol-level fix using explicit terms, event identities, and idempotent command application. Explain which fields belong in signed or hashed provenance and which are local transport details. Sketch Rust types for Term, EventId, IndexedEvent, and an apply result without using ambiguous primitive aliases. Describe election and recovery behavior when nodes disagree about the last committed index. Include property tests for duplicate delivery, reordering, failover between receive and index, and replay from durable storage. Discuss whether exactly-once delivery is necessary or whether at-least-once transport plus deterministic deduplication is sufficient. Identify the state that must survive process restart and a bounded strategy for retaining deduplication records. Finally, propose observability fields that let an operator reconstruct a failover without logging sensitive request content, and state the safety and liveness properties separately.

Plan a multi-step OpenCode-style task that must use tools safely. The user asks to update a configuration parser, migrate existing examples, run tests, and summarize the result, but the repository has unrelated uncommitted edits. Describe the exact sequence of searches, file reads, patches, and verification commands you would perform. The parser accepts a JSON object with version, model, cache policy, and optional parallelism fields. A version two document must reject unknown cache policies and conflicting tensor and pipeline parallel settings while continuing to read version one documents. Define a strict schema and a migration function with exhaustive types. Show representative valid and invalid examples, but keep them original and short. Explain how you preserve unrelated work, how you avoid destructive source control commands, and how you react if formatting changes files outside the requested scope. Include tests for forward compatibility, error messages, deterministic serialization, and an absent optional field. When discussing tool calls, separate read-only discovery from writes and explain what outcome justifies each call. Finish with a final response suitable for the user that leads with the implemented behavior, names the files changed, reports only tests actually observed, and calls out one deliberately unsupported ambiguity.

Calibration case 3 of 4. Treat this as an independent repository task; preserve its constraints and reason through concrete evidence before the next case.

Review an original C++ component that manages fixed-size GPU staging buffers. A BufferLease contains a pointer, byte count, pool index, and monotonically increasing generation. Move construction acquires ownership correctly, but move assignment overwrites an existing live lease without returning it, and a completion callback captures the old object by reference. Explain the lifetime and reuse bugs in detail, including a plausible sequence that corrupts a later transfer. Propose a small RAII redesign with deleted copying, noexcept moves, explicit release, generation validation, and a callback token that cannot dangle. Supply compact header-level pseudocode and describe which operations need synchronization. Consider whether an atomic generation alone is sufficient when callback execution and pool destruction race. Define unit tests for self-move, move assignment into a live lease, callback after reuse, pool shutdown, and exception paths. Add one sanitizer-oriented integration test and explain what it can and cannot prove. Preserve performance by avoiding allocation on the normal acquire and release path. End by identifying the narrowest safe patch, ABI considerations, and telemetry that would reveal stale completion events in production. Do not depend on external library text or undocumented compiler behavior.

Calibration case 4 of 4. Treat this as an independent repository task; preserve its constraints and reason through concrete evidence before the next case.

You receive a long diagnostic bundle from an inference benchmark containing request timestamps, GPU utilization samples, per-layer kernel durations, cache hit counters, and interconnect byte counters. The benchmark reports high steady decode speed but sporadic forty-second first-token delays. Design a disciplined analysis that does not confuse correlation with causation. Start by defining a normalized timeline and the phases of admission, tokenization, prefix lookup, prefill, first decode, and streaming. Explain how to align clocks from separate processes and how to detect missing or duplicated samples. Propose queries that compare cold and warm requests, cache-busted prompts, repeated long prompts, and simultaneous clients. Include hypotheses involving compilation, CPU expert page faults, allocator pressure, synchronization, and prefix-cache contention, with a falsifying observation for each. Describe a compact receipt format that records configuration hashes, model identity, GPU topology, and phase percentiles without storing prompt text. Explain how median, tail latency, and throughput can move in opposite directions. End with a ranked next-run plan that changes one factor at a time and a warning against accepting a fast run if semantic output, both-GPU activity, or request completion is invalid.

Design tests for a page-based compressed attention cache with three logical tiers: an exact recent window, four-token compressed history, and one-hundred-twenty-eight-token compressed history. Physical storage uses packed unsigned codes with per-group scale and zero, while the recent window stays in high precision. The allocator translates logical token locations into tier-specific page locations and CUDA graphs replay with fixed buffers but changing sequence lengths. State the essential invariants before writing examples. Develop property-based tests for location translation, boundary tokens, page rollover, partial final groups, and allocation reuse. Add numerical parity tests against a clear CPU reference for packing, dequantization, score computation, and mixed-tier online softmax. Include adversarial rows such as constant values, large outliers, negative-only groups, smallest nonzero scale, and every possible two-bit code. Explain how to test graph replay without accidentally validating capture-time inputs twice. Add concurrency tests for two requests sharing physical pages only through correct reference counting. Define failure messages that reveal layer, tier, logical position, and seed. Finally, separate tests required for merge approval from expensive nightly stress tests, and explain why a memory-footprint assertion belongs beside numerical parity rather than only in a benchmark.
